content.value_statement: SpecDD repositories can be hard to enter without knowing the active bootstrap and authority model. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a read-only orientation pass before later work.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a repository has a root .specdd/bootstrap.md file.
Reads the active bootstrap chain in the documented order.
Identifies the root or main project spec named by the bootstrap files.
Inspects top-level specs and repository shape for orientation.
Checks git status so later work can distinguish existing changes.
Reports concise readiness context without editing files.
limitations: Does not adopt SpecDD into repositories that lack a bootstrap file.
Does not edit, implement, refactor, or review code during orientation.
Does not replace normal SpecDD spec-chain resolution for a later concrete task.
Does not treat nearby specs as authority unless selected by bootstrap, spec, or user request.

use_cases.title: Prepare for a Follow-Up Coding Task
use_cases.description: Read the bootstrap chain and summarize project authority before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Onboard an AI Assistant to a SpecDD Repository
use_cases.description: Give an assistant enough project context to answer basic readiness questions without changing files.

use_cases.title: Confirm Repository Readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether a repository is already a SpecDD project and identify blockers before assigning work.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Orientation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use specdd-orient to get oriented in this repository. Do not edit files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a safe read-only orientation pass.

prompt_templates.title: Readiness Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Orient in this SpecDD project and summarize the bootstrap files read, main project authority, and any blocker to follow-up work.
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants concise readiness context before assigning a task.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Spec Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use specdd-orient, then inspect only the top-level specs that affect repository authority for the next task I describe.
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs orientation with limited scope before later planning.

prompt_templates.title: Team Handoff Preparation
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a read-only SpecDD orientation pass and produce a short handoff note for another assistant that will perform the next concrete task.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow where one assistant prepares context for another.

output_examples.input: Orient in this SpecDD repository before I ask for changes.
output_examples.output: Orientation complete. Read the bootstrap chain, identified the main project spec, inspected top-level authority files, and checked git status. No immediate blocker found.

output_examples.input: Check whether this repository is ready for SpecDD-guided work.
output_examples.output: The repository has a root bootstrap file, so it appears to be a SpecDD project. The active authority comes from the bootstrap chain and the named project spec.

output_examples.input: Prepare a short handoff for a future implementation task.
output_examples.output: Handoff ready. The next assistant should rerun normal SpecDD spec-chain resolution for the concrete target path before making edits.

best_practices: Use this skill before a concrete task when the assistant lacks SpecDD context.
Keep the orientation report short and focused on readiness.
Rerun normal spec-chain resolution before any later file edits.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to make implementation changes.
Do not treat orientation context as permanent write authority.
Do not continue when the repository lacks .specdd/bootstrap.md unless the user asks for adoption.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It orients an assistant in an existing SpecDD project by reading bootstrap and relevant authority files.

faq.question: Does it change files?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly limits the assistant to read-only orientation.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before asking for later work when the assistant needs SpecDD project context.

faq.question: Can it adopt SpecDD into a new project?
faq.answer: No. It should stop if .specdd/bootstrap.md is missing unless the user requests a separate adoption flow.

faq.question: Does it replace task-specific spec resolution?
faq.answer: No. Later concrete tasks still need normal SpecDD spec-chain resolution for the target path or behavior.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
